body:
This decoupling makes sense to me — one knob spanning three components with different heartbeat/health-check budgets forces exactly the kind of lockstep tuning you describe.

If you're not already planning to implement it yourself, I'd be happy to pick it up: add `[triggerer]` / `[dag_processor]` overrides that fall back to the current `[workers]` values for backwards compatibility, wire them where each component builds its API client retry policy, and cover the fallback semantics with tests. And if you'd rather drive it, I'm glad to help review instead.

issue.title: Decouple [workers] execution_api_retries from Dag Processor and Triggerer

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
This PR decouples Execution API retry configuration for workers, triggerer and dag processor.

Previously all three components used the same `[workers]` options.

Triggerer and dag processor can now define these options in their own `[triggerer]` and `[dag_processor]` sections.

Each option falls back independently to its corresponding `[workers]` value when it isn't configured. This also allows partial overrides. For example, the Triggerer can override only `execution_api_retries` while continuing to use the worker values for the minimum and maximum retry wait.
Workers continue to use `[workers]` by default.

closes: #73196
